title: Private deploy networking - debug breadcrumbs
notes:
Incident summary:
- Feb 14 2026: customer private deployment in eu-west-1 reports 5xx errors from managed hosted services (metrics ingestion + control-plane calls). Symptoms intermittent but frequent after ~09:30 UTC.
- Affects a subset of nodes in customer VPC peered to our infra. Not a global outage.

Initial triage (what I ran):
- ssh into bastion (eu-west-1): ssh -i ~/.ssh/prv-deploy.pem ubuntu@34.56.78.90
- kubectl (remote kubecontext): kubectl get nodes -o wide -n redwood
- Check services: kubectl get svc -n redwood --selector=app=control-plane -o yaml
- DNS check from inside customer node: dig +short api.internal.redwood.local @10.0.2.5 -> (sometimes NXDOMAIN, sometimes IP)
- curl test to control plane via internal IP: curl -v --resolve "api.internal.redwood.local:443:10.20.30.45" https://api.internal.redwood.local/health
  - Observed: connect to 10.20.30.45 port 443: Connection timed out (intermittent)

Packet-level checks:
- tcpdump on node eth0: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.20.30.45 and port 443 -w /tmp/trace.pcap
  - Captured SYNs leaving node, no SYN-ACK returned on some flows.
- traceroute -n 10.20.30.45 -> shows traffic goes to customer NAT and then blackholes (last hop * * *)

Egress / Network ACLs / Firewall checks:
- iptables -L -v on node -> no obvious DROP rules for port 443.
- ip route show -> default via 10.0.0.1 dev eth0
- aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0abc123 -> found a recently added NACL rule (added 2026-02-13) that DENYs ephemeral high ports range 32768-61000 (suspect)
  - Rule: DENY TCP 32768-61000 from 0.0.0.0/0 (applied to private-subnet-a)
  - This lines up with ephemeral port usage for connections from the node to our control plane.

DNS anomalies:
- nslookup api.internal.redwood.local 10.0.2.5 -> sometimes returns CNAME to hosted api.redwood.local, sometimes NXDOMAIN.
- Observed race when kube-dns restarted around the same time as scheduled patch on host (02:58 UTC) -> clients cached NXDOMAIN briefly.
- dig +trace shows delegation to private zone in Route53: ZONE-ID matches customer-account-managed zone. No TTL misconfig noted.

TLS checks:
- openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.45:443 -servername api.internal.redwood.local
  - Observed handshake succeeded when connection made. Certificate CN=api.redwood.local, chain ok.
  - But in failed flows there is no handshake (SYN only), so TLS not reached.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Recent NACL change is intermittently blocking ephemeral source ports -> manifesting as connection timeouts (strong evidence from AWS NACL deny rule and traceroute blackhole).
2) DNS instability (kube-dns restarts + private zone flapping) causing some clients to try unreachable endpoints (moderate evidence: NXDOMAIN spikes).
3) MTU / fragmentation between VPCs / peering causing SYN drops for certain path (low evidence so far; would expect ICMP fragmentation messages).
4) Security group rule race during autoscaling where newly created ENIs lack correct SGs (possible; check ENI attach logs).

Commands/results of note (raw snippets):
- curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://api.internal.redwood.local/health --resolve "api.internal.redwood.local:443:10.20.30.45"
  * Trying 10.20.30.45:443...
  * connect to 10.20.30.45 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
  * Failed to connect to api.internal.redwood.local port 443: Connection timed out
- dig +short api.internal.redwood.local @10.0.2.5
  -> (sometimes) 10.20.30.45
  -> (sometimes) <empty> (NXDOMAIN)
- sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 tcp and host 10.20.30.45
  12:41:02.123456 IP 10.0.4.32.43210 > 10.20.30.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7]
  12:41:02.125678 IP 10.0.4.32.43210 > 10.20.30.45.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,...]
  (no SYN-ACK seen)

Cross-checks with our infra team:
- Asked infra to inspect peering route tables and NAT gateway metrics. Peering routes appear correct, but CloudWatch for NAT GW shows spikes in connection errors around 09:30 UTC.
- Infra confirmed a runbook change on Feb 13 that tightened NACLs to meet a compliance request. That aligns with the NACL deny rule found.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Reverted NACL change in private-subnet-a at 12:05 UTC (rollback): removed DENY for ephemeral ports.
- Post-rollback: successful pings/curl from same nodes to 10.20.30.45 within 2 minutes. Error rate dropped to baseline.

Root cause (working conclusion):
- Human-introduced NACL rule denying ephemeral source ports (32768-61000) blocked return traffic for TCP flows to our control plane, causing TCP handshake to fail on many flows. DNS flakiness exacerbated the symptom window but was not the primary cause.

Notes for permanent fix / follow-ups:
- Action items:
  1) Policy: add guardrail to prevent NACL denies that include ephemeral port ranges for private subnets used by control-plane traffic. (Owner: Samir)
  2) Add automated pre-deploy check that simulates outbound ephemeral TCP flows to known internal endpoints before applying NACL changes. (Owner: Leah)
  3) Improve observability: create CloudWatch metric alert for NACL denies or NAT connection error spikes. (Owner: Maya)
  4) Document runbook: rollback steps + verification commands (this doc + link to RDW-2391). (Owner: Alex)
  5) Investigate DNS POD restarts cause and reduce churn during maintenance windows. (Owner: Eng-SRE)

Quick verification checklist (to include in runbook):
- From a node in private-subnet-a: curl -v --resolve "api.internal.redwood.local:443:10.20.30.45" https://api.internal.redwood.local/health
- tcpdump to confirm SYN->SYN-ACK handshake
- aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=<vpc-id> | grep -i 32768
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns --watch

Notes to self / lessons learned:
- NACLs are stateless -> must allow ephemeral ranges for return traffic. Easy to forget when tightening policies.
- DNS flapping will amplify a small networking regression into perceived larger outage. minimize churn during infra changes.
- Keep a short incident checklist for private deploy customers (we had some friction moving from detection -> rollback).

Attachments / traces saved:
- /var/tmp/trace-2026-02-14-nodeA.pcap (tcpdump capture)
- CloudWatch NATGW metrics snapshot 2026-02-14-09:00-10:30 (S3 link in RDW-2391)

Status: rollback applied, monitoring shows stable as of 2026-02-14 12:30 UTC. Leaving this as draft for runbook write-up and postmortem notes.

Next steps timeline:
- 2026-02-21: Postmortem draft (Alex)
- 2026-02-24: Runbook + guardrail PR (Samir / Leah)
- 2026-03-01: Follow-up review with Eng-SRE and Product (confirm no similar NACLs in other accounts)
